references.text: Expands on the punishment for sacrificing children to Molech and describes how God will turn against those who do this.
Forbids Israelites from worshipping God in the same way as the nations, who burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
Prohibits letting one's son or daughter pass through the fire, as part of a list of pagan customs.
Solomon built a high place for Molech, showing violation of this commandment.
King Ahaz let his son pass through the fire according to the abominations of the nations.
Israel let their sons and daughters pass through the fire, which led to their exile.
King Manasseh let his son pass through the fire and profaned the name of the Lord.
King Josiah destroyed Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom to prevent anyone from letting their children pass through the fire to Molech.
The prophet Jeremiah condemns Judah for building high places for Baal and sacrificing their children to Molech.
Ezekiel accuses Israel of profaning God's name by letting their children pass through the fire.
Ezekiel condemns Israel for sacrificing their children to idols, thereby desecrating God's sanctuary.
Stephen quotes the prophet Amos and mentions Molech in his speech about Israel's history with idolatry.
